criteria.reasoning: The sheet dates G-1 as “2026-01-02” and places it in tax year “2026.” The Marchettis’ receipt says the shares were credited on “January 2, 2026,” and does not use a 2025 gift date.

The deliverable lists G-1’s valuation basis as the January 2 closing price of $62.05 and states the gift value is $24,820.00. The criterion requires the January 2 high-low mean of $62.67 and a gift value of $25,068.00, and explicitly fails any other figure.
The Delacroix gift is dated “2025-12-30,” placed in tax year “2025,” and valued at “$9,557.50.” The deliverable shows the required basis: “(38.62 + 37.84) ÷ 2 = $38.23 × 250 = $9,557.50.”

The sheet dates the Fenn gift as “2026-01-05,” assigns it to tax year “2026,” and says the certificate “reached us on 2026-01-05.” The Fenn receipt likewise says the certificate was “received on January 5, 2026,” rather than using the required postmark date of 2025-12-31.
The deliverable values G-3 at “$10,370.40,” using the January 5 mean of $86.42. The criterion requires $10,149.60, based on the December 31 mean of $84.58, and explicitly says $10,370.40 fails.
The gift-entry sheet dates G-4 to “2025-12-31” and places it in tax year “2025.” The notes also confirm the shares were credited to the fund account on 2025-12-31, the date of gift.
The deliverable values G-4 at “$21,275.32,” using the “Public offering price” of $26.19 per share. The criterion requires $20,048.67 based on the $24.68 net asset value, so it fails.

The G-2 receipt states, “As you asked, the value of your gift on that date was $9,557.50,” which is a dollar value for the securities. The criterion requires that none of the receipts or other donor-facing wording state a value, including Delacroix’s receipt.

Each receipt states the share count and names the security: for example, G-1 acknowledges “400 shares of Quarry Point Industries, Inc. common stock,” and G-3 gives “120 shares of Ostrander Railcar Corporation common stock.” G-4 states “812.345 shares of Lantern Ridge Balanced Fund, Class A,” the required fund share count and security.
Each of the four receipts says, “No goods or services were provided in exchange for your gift.” None says otherwise. The criterion is satisfied.
